content:
Yes, when you run:

```bash
pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>
```

the virtual environment named `<venv-name>` will be deleted entirely. This means that the directory containing the virtual environment, along with all installed packages in that env, will be removed.

In other words, all packages installed inside that virtual environment will be deleted because the whole venv folder is removed.

**Note:** Make sure you do not have important data or files inside the virtual environment directory before deleting it. If you want to keep a list of installed packages to recreate the environment later, you can run:

```bash
pip freeze > requirements.txt
```

inside the venv before deleting it.
